item.title: Geothermal Startup Raises $144 Million to Drill Superhot Rocks
item.description: Geothermal startup Quaise Energy raised $144 million to develop technology for drilling superhot rocks.

item.title: Germany Recorded 5,000 Excess Deaths in Late-June Heat Wave
item.description: Germany recorded more than 5,000 excess deaths during the late-June heat wave, according to preliminary data from the Federal Statistical Office.

item.title: Faster, Fiercer Wildfires Are Testing Evacuation Plans
item.description: As heat waves fuel more intense blazes, fire officials are rethinking how to safely empty hard-to-escape neighborhoods

item.title: Germany Plans to Cut €2.1 Billion in Heat Pump Subsidies by 2030
item.description: Germany plans to cut generous subsidies for low-carbon heat pumps by about €2.1 billion ($2.4 billion) in the coming years, as it aims to make some budget savings while raising spending on defense and security.

item.title: ECB Rolls Out Haircuts on Collateral as Climate Risks Grow
item.description: The European Central Bank is imposing additional so-called haircuts on collateral that poses a climate risk, to guard against possible losses.

item.title: Mumbai Struggles to Cope as Record Rains Lash Financial Hub
item.description: Mumbai’s wettest start to July in decades killed at least 13 people in the city and its adjoining areas and caused widespread disruption for millions of residents, raising questions about the quality of infrastructure in India’s financial hub.

item.title: Europe’s Latest Heat Wave Raises Pressure on Water, Power Grids
item.description: Temperatures are soaring across western Europe as the third major heat wave to hit the region this year fuels wildfire danger, strains water supplies and tests power grids.

item.title: Banks’ Exposure to Heat-Related Losses Faces Scrutiny in EU
item.description: Europe’s bank watchdog will look at how exposed lenders are to heat-related risks, as temperature records keep getting broken.

item.title: JPMorgan Relaxes Return-to-Office Rules During London Heat Wave
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. has relaxed some of the finance industry’s strictest return-to-office requirements for its London staff, after the UK capital sweltered through record-high temperatures.

item.title: Super Typhoon Set to Bring More Heavy Rain to China This Week
item.description: A powerful typhoon that battered Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands is maintaining significant strength as it tracks over warm Pacific Ocean waters toward Taiwan and southeastern China.

item.title: Founder of Brookfield-Backed Avaada Seeks $750 Million Loan
item.description: The founder of Avaada Group, one of India’s largest clean-energy company, is planning to borrow about $750 million from a group of global lenders to refinance the firm’s existing debt, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: South32’s Arizona Zinc and Manganese Mine to Get US Approval
item.description: The Trump administration is set to authorize South32 Ltd.’s planned $2 billion zinc and manganese mine in Arizona on Tuesday.

item.title: Carney Cites NATO, Melting Arctic as Germany Wins Submarine Contract
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney stressed the importance of defending against growing threats in the melting Arctic as he picked a German-Norwegian offer to build a new fleet of submarines for Canada’s navy.

item.title: Flood Risk Doesn’t Matter as Bargain Houses Tempt NZ Buyers
item.description: New Zealand’s flood-prone homes are outperforming the rest of the country’s moribund housing market, as buyers chase lower prices and shrug off climate risks.

item.title: Floods in Southern China’s Guangxi Kill Two, Thousands Evacuated
item.description: Flooding triggered by Typhoon Maysak has sparked two deaths in southern China and forced thousands of people to evacuate, with more rains expected through mid-week, according to state media reports.

item.title: Brookfield Approved as Lead Bidder, Lender to Polish Solar Firm
item.description: Private equity firm Brookfield Corp. won a key court ruling against funds managed by Joh. Berenberg, Gossler & Co. in the battle for control of bankrupt solar-power company GoldenPeaks Poland Holding Ltd.

item.title: Dogger Bank Wind Farm Challenges UK Approval of Nearby RWE Site
item.description: The owners of the world’s biggest offshore wind farm petitioned a UK judge to challenge the government’s decision to approve the development of another major project nearby, potentially throwing the new one into doubt.

item.title: Heavy Rain Triggers Flood Watches in New York and Eastern US
item.description: Heavy rain will trigger flood watches from Ohio to southeastern Massachusetts, including New York City, and as far south as North Carolina, according to the National Weather Service.

item.title: Europe Faces Weeks of Extreme Heat as Fire and Power Risks Build
item.description: Western Europe is bracing for the summer’s third major heat wave, fueling dangerous wildfire conditions and straining power systems across the region.

item.title: Climate Extremes Are Becoming More Extreme, Worrying Scientists
item.description: Heat, sea level rise, polar melting: They’re all picking up pace.

item.title: Teeth That Can Cut Cans: The Ravenous Fish Invading Greek Seas
item.description: Climate change is prompting the puffer fish to migrate from the tropical waters of the Indian Ocean to the Mediterranean.

item.title: Extreme Heat Isn't the Only Climate Impact Shocking Scientists
item.description: For the full experience visit: Extreme Heat Isn't the Only Climate Impact Shocking Scientists

item.title: El Niño Threatens To Fuel Coal Power Surge in India, Study Says
item.description: A super El Niño risks straining India’s power grid more than any other electricity network globally and would slow the country’s shift away from coal, according to a new study.

item.title: More Investors Add Pressure on EU to Ban Drilling in the Arctic
item.description: Six institutional investors joined a call urging the European Union to maintain its opposition against further Arctic oil and gas expansion, saying the EU needs to continue to commit to its green transition.

item.title: Europe’s Heat Wave Is Bright Spot for China’s Portable AC Makers
item.description: As heat records shattered across Europe in the last weeks of June and indoor temperatures rose to uncomfortable levels, many of the continent’s residents sought immediate relief in the form of portable air conditioner units.

item.title: US Northern Marianas Threatened by Second Super Typhoon in 2026
item.description: Guam and the Northern Marianas Islands are being threatened by a super typhoon for the second time this year.

item.title: Drivers Shun Premium Gas in Favor of Regular as Prices Bite
item.description: Drivers across the US, including some behind the wheel of performance vehicles, are switching from premium gasoline to regular in a search for savings as fuel prices remain elevated.

item.title: New York Thunderstorms Raise Flood Risk as Heat Dissipates in US
item.description: New York City will have a cooler, soggier Sunday now that the massive heat dome across the US East that taxed power grids and snarled transit has started to crack, but temperatures in Washington and points south will still remain sultry through Sunday.

item.title: Greece Offers Bounty to Catch Ravenous Fish Lured by Warming Sea
item.description: Stavros Moraitis has spent more than three decades fishing in the azure waters off the Greek island of Milos. He’s used to competition from rare monk seals, but now global warming has brought a rival with a far more voracious appetite: the silver-cheeked puffer fish.

item.title: Wildfire Near Thessaloniki in Greece Sparks Evacuations
item.description: THESSALONIKI, Greece (AP) — A fast-moving wildfire broke out Saturday evening near the suburbs of Thessaloniki, Greece's second largest city, the country's fire service said, and residents of three small suburbs north of the city were told to evacuate.
